coverages.description: Live coverage of the Cockroach Janta Party's protest movement — detentions, ultimatums, court cases, INDIA-bloc actions and on-ground developments in Delhi.
coverages.title: CJP Protest 2.0
coverages.current_summary: CJP's 24-hour ultimatum to Delhi Police expired on Oct 13 without protest permission; police registered an FIR against co-conveners Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka for alleged trespass at Jantar Mantar and breach of their one-year peace bond, while the INDIA bloc escalated — Rahul Gandhi pledged to challenge Jantar Mantar's de-notification, proposed an early-November Ramlila Maidan rally, and told leaders to be ready to mobilise within 24 hours. Late Tuesday added two flashpoints: Dipke publicly challenged CJI Surya Kant over law-and-order remarks (he's expected in Delhi Oct 14), and a journalist who says she is three months pregnant alleged Gandhi pushed her during the Oct 12 march — amplified by the BJP, denied by Congress. Early Wednesday (~2:30 AM IST), Delhi Police moved the detained leaders — Ranka, Das and others — out of Jaffarpur Kalan police station; their destination is unknown.

coverages.description: Live coverage of the Houthi-Saudi escalation — missile and drone strikes on Riyadh and oil sites, airport and airspace closures, Saudi/coalition retaliation, US moves and diplomatic developments.
coverages.title: Houthi-Riyadh Escalation
coverages.current_summary: Tuesday Oct 13 saw the sharpest escalation yet: Houthis struck Aramco's Dhahran HQ (limited fire in an admin building, no injuries) and fired on Riyadh, where the coalition says it downed three drones over northern Riyadh plus three missiles and two drones aimed at Riyadh and Aramco; the coalition followed its Sanaa fuel-site evacuation order with fresh airstrikes on Sanaa (Houthis claim 2 killed, 2 injured at the fuel hub), while Houthi strikes on Taiz killed 6 and injured 18, and four people in Riyadh were injured by falling debris from the intercepted night volley — the first reported Riyadh injuries. Trump blamed Iran and hinted at US military action after the Nov 3 midterms; Saudi Arabia's Cabinet warned of 'consequences' and launched an inquiry into the air-defence gaps; Egypt pressed Iran to halt the attacks; airlines kept ferrying aircraft out of Riyadh, and King Khalid airport remains closed till Oct 17.

coverages.description: Live coverage of the Russia-Ukraine war focused on the 'Energy Ceasefire' — strikes on energy infrastructure by either side, ceasefire claims and violations, Kremlin/White House/Kyiv statements, EU sanctions and oil-market fallout.
coverages.title: Russia-Ukraine War & Energy Ceasefire
coverages.current_summary: Trump's claimed 'energy ceasefire' is fraying: after Russia's Defence Ministry reported no energy targets hit overnight Oct 12-13, Russian drones sank a cargo ship off Bulgaria with 11 sailors missing, and late Tuesday ballistic missiles hit Kyiv targeting thermal plant No. 4 (Darnytska CHP-4), killing 1 and injuring 13. Zelensky confirmed to NPR that the Trump administration did threaten to cut off intelligence-sharing over Ukraine's refinery strikes — contradicting Trump's same-day denial — and counter-offered a Ukrainian 'diesel deal' to Trump's Russian diesel arrangement; France seized the suspected shadow-fleet tanker DF Peak near Réunion (Moscow called it 'piracy'), while Germany and Canada rejected the US-brokered diesel deal. Late Tuesday, 12 bipartisan senators urged Trump to rescind the Russian diesel deal, and WaPo reported the US and Europe are drafting a joint four-pillar peace plan (reconstruction/compensation, security guarantees, a frontline ceasefire, plus an energy deal).

coverages.description: Live coverage of hurricane and tropical-storm activity impacting North America — NHC advisories, storm formation and intensity changes, watches and warnings, landfalls, casualties, damage and outage numbers, evacuations, closures and recovery.
coverages.location: North America (Atlantic basin, Gulf of Mexico, US Gulf/East coasts, Mexico's Pacific coast)
coverages.title: Hurricane Activity Impacting North America
coverages.current_summary: Tropical Storm Trudy formed off southern Mexico on Oct 13 (40 mph in NHC Advisory 2, ~490 mi SSE of Acapulco) with rapid intensification to a major hurricane forecast by Friday; Hurricane Simon stays a Category 1 drifting offshore — mainland Mexico watches were lifted (Advisory 26) and Puerto Vallarta airport reopened, but NHC's evening discussion shifted Simon's track to a weekend coast approach with a possible Sunday inland crossing over Sonora — while damage tallies keep rising across Guerrero, Colima and Baja California Sur. The White House approved federal emergency declarations for Florida and Alabama ahead of Isaias's landfall; no active Atlantic cyclones after the Cabo Verde disturbance fizzled. Isaias recovery reached ~95% of impacted-area customers restored as of Tuesday evening (~57,000 still out), Florida rolled out $10M in zero-interest business loans plus farm loans and SNAP aid for the Panhandle, and catastrophe modeler Verisk issued the first industry insured-loss estimate: $1B–$2B for onshore property.

coverages.title: U.S.–Iran Conflict & Strait of Hormuz
coverages.description: Live coverage of the U.S.–Iran confrontation — military posturing, strikes or threats, Strait of Hormuz shipping incidents and closure threats, Iranian statements, US administration moves, oil-market and diplomatic fallout.
coverages.current_summary: Strait of Hormuz shipping attacks escalated Oct 11-13: UKMTO documented six vessels struck on Oct 11 alone — the war's highest single-day total — and on Tuesday confirmed BOTH a tanker and a container ship hit by unknown projectiles in the strait, with Iran's Army Navy also claiming a 'violating' tanker caught fire east of the strait; UKMTO also back-filled an Oct 7 strike on the chemical/oil tanker Acers off Qatar — the first deep-Gulf attack in nearly a month, with casualties reported. The UK blamed the IRGC for the RAF Fairford drone plot with 29 nations backing the attribution, while Trump claimed all 159 Iranian naval vessels were sunk, said the US 'might have gone too far' targeting Iran's leadership, and said the war 'will end very soon'; Brent holds near $105-106.

coverages.title: 2026 US Midterm Elections
coverages.description: Polls, early voting, key House/Senate/gubernatorial races, and campaign moves ahead of the Nov 3, 2026 US midterm elections.
coverages.current_summary: Three weeks out from the Nov 3 midterms, Democrats remain strong favorites to retake the House — Fox News' latest Power Rankings moved ~20 races leftward to a 219-198 Dem edge with 18 toss-ups — with an 8-9 point generic-ballot lead (Republican pollster John McLaughlin countered late Tuesday that his firm's generic ballot has Democrats only +5) and a 43-35 Gallup party-image edge; the Senate is tightening — a new Quantus poll has Texas effectively tied (Paxton 47.2%, Talarico 46.7%) and MS NOW moved Kansas to Lean R (Minnesota to Lean D) — as the Texas governor race flipped back to Abbott 48-47 in a ReconMR/Siena poll reversing the Oct 6 YouGov read, Hochul and Blakeman met in NY's only gubernatorial debate, Trump campaigns in Ohio and Kansas ahead of an Oct 19 Wichita rally, and DHS agents raided Rep. Ilhan Omar's D.C. home early Oct 12 in an immigration-fraud probe. Late Tuesday brought fresh polls: North Carolina's Senate race has Cooper +14 in WRAL/SurveyUSA (54-40, his strongest yet), the Texas Senate lead narrowed to Talarico 48, Paxton 44 in ReconMR/Siena, and Rhode Island's governor race tightened to Foulkes 44, Block 35; Trump expanded his rally blitz to Kentucky and North Carolina alongside the Oct 19 Wichita stop.
